name: Grande Mosquée de Bobo-Dioulasso
subtitle: The Grande Mosquée of Bobo-Dioulasso, also called the mosque of Dioulassoba, is an adobe mosque in the Sudano-Sahelian style, built of local materials.

facts.label: Architectural style
facts.value: Sudano-Sahelian adobe mosque, second in size only to the Great Mosque of Djenné (per a peer-reviewed article)

facts.label: Description
facts.value: Described as a masterpiece of the Sudano-Sahelian adobe style

facts.label: Materials
facts.value: Built of local materials, notably earth (terre cuite, as reported)

facts.label: Form
facts.value: Its design sets it apart from mosques of Arab-Muslim inspiration

facts.label: Date (Minister of Culture)
facts.value: Built in 1893, according to Culture Minister Abdoul Karim Sango

facts.label: Rehabilitation cost
facts.value: Rehabilitation project launched 18 November 2016, estimated at 527,831,073 CFA francs

facts.label: Handover
facts.value: Handed back to the Muslim community on 5 September 2019

facts.label: Ownership
facts.value: Described by the minister as a good belonging to the community

facts.label: Condition before works
facts.value: Described as heavily degraded and needing rehabilitation

facts.label: Minaret collapse
facts.value: Part of the minaret fell on 8 August 2021 and the rest on 13 August 2021

facts.label: Earlier collapses
facts.value: Local sources say parts of the mosque began collapsing in October 2018, during rehabilitation

parts.text: The Grande Mosquée of Bobo-Dioulasso, also called the mosque of Dioulassoba, is an adobe mosque in the Sudano-Sahelian style, built of local materials. Sources date it to 1880 or 1893. It was rehabilitated between 2016 and 2019 and handed back to the Muslim community on 5 September 2019, but part of its minaret collapsed in August 2021.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
